items.explanation: 80-year-old woman (DOB 1945-10-26) with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note from 2025-09-12 through 2026-05-28. Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin only; there is no current or past anticoagulant order in the chart. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: congestive heart failure (I5040/I5043, hypertensive heart disease with heart failure I110), hypertension (I10/4019), age 80 (2 points), type 2 diabetes (E119/E11649), prior cerebral infarction/TIA (V1254, I69322/I69351 deficits following cerebral infarction, 2 points), vascular disease (coronary atherosclerosis I2510, old MI 412) and female sex. Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is absent; aspirin is not an acceptable substitute. Needs anticoagulation review.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list, above the 20 mg/day maximum advised for QT safety in older patients) is current (order 7f787d30, 2026-05-29 to 2026-12-25). The most recent ECG, 104821039 of 2023-11-10, shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT about 485 ms and Bazett QTc about 521 ms (>=500 ms), up from QTc about 434 ms on the 2020-06-17 tracing. Prescriber review is required. Most recent potassium 4.5 mmol/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01) are normal.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) is current (order c6f532e9, 2026-08-22 to 2027-01-05) in a 95-year-old woman. The most recent ECG, 101515306 of 2022-04-27, shows sinus bradycardia at 58/min with QT about 520 ms and Bazett QTc about 518 ms (>=500 ms), versus QTc about 429 ms on the AF tracing of 2022-04-06. Prescriber review is required and no ECG has been obtained since 2022. Most recent electrolytes (2026-02-14): potassium 4.1 mmol/L, magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (low-normal). She is also on warfarin, whose effect amiodarone potentiates.

Amiodarone (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (first outpatient order e578297f; the drug is absent from the 2025-08-02 medication list and appears on the 2025-11-10 list). Started after 2025-09-01 and before 2026-03-01, so the 30-day window of the 2025-09-01 memo applies: ECG due by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met. (That ECG shows QTc about 516 ms and is the subject of a separate QT safety item.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-02-12 (first order in the chart, cbe91d0f, authored at that visit). Start date is on/after 2025-09-01 and before 2026-03-01, so the 30-day window applies: ECG due by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was obtained 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start - within the window, so completed. That tracing shows sinus rhythm with QTc about 397 ms.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (first order c17946a1; drug absent from the 2025-12-15 medication list). Started on/after 2026-03-01, so the revised 14-day window applies: ECG due by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was obtained 2026-03-07, 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met (sinus rhythm, QTc about 378 ms).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (first order 88943096, authored at that visit). Started after 2026-03-01, so the revised 14-day window applies: ECG was due by 2026-04-24. The only ECG in the chart, 107859369, was recorded 2026-04-29 - 19 days after the start and 5 days after the deadline - so the requirement was not met within the required time and is overdue as of 2026-09-24. (That late ECG showed sinus rhythm, QTc about 376 ms.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (order 4dde586a; the drug is absent from the 2026-06-24 medication list and appears on the 2026-08-01 list). Started after 2026-03-01, so an ECG was due within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25 (106035722, which predates the start), so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (order f757652a; absent from the 2026-02-27 medication list). Started after 2026-03-01, so an ECG was due within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. The telephone note of 2026-08-25 (DocumentReference 5e12a8aa-0439-53cd-a194-cc1a277d296d) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - within the window - but the report was requested by fax and has not been received, and no ECG for this patient exists in the chart. Whether the requirement was met cannot be determined until that outside tracing is obtained.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-09-15 (order 9db19264; first outpatient haloperidol order, drug absent from the 2026-06-05 medication list). Started after 2026-03-01, so an ECG is due within 14 days, by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since 2025-03-09; as of the 2026-09-24 review the monitoring ECG is not yet overdue but should be scheduled.

At the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr Kessler documented 'INR today 1.6, subtherapeutic. Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR' - a warfarin dose change made by a clinic clinician after 2026-03-01, so an INR was required within 7 days (by 2026-09-08). INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05 (Observation d6b3bad5), within the window, so the requirement was met.

48-year-old man (DOB 1978-02-27) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation carried in the problem list of every cardiology clinic note from 2025-07-19 to 2026-06-12 (dysrhythmia also coded 2025-06-17). Current medications are famotidine and pantoprazole only; no anticoagulant order is active and none has been ordered since the 2025 admissions. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2: heart failure (congestive heart failure 4280 / acute systolic heart failure 42821 / cardiomyopathy 4254, Feb 2025) and hypertension (4019). A score of 2 in a man is a guideline indication for oral anticoagulation, so the absence of therapy needs review. Note the chart also carries 'long-term current use of anticoagulants' (V5861, Jun 2025), which is not supported by any active order.

The anticoagulation clinic note of 2026-09-10 by L. Nguyen, PharmD documents a dose change made under the clinic protocol: home INR 3.4, warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily. A clinic pharmacist dose change after 2026-03-01 requires an INR within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-17. No INR has been resulted since 2026-08-22 (2.6), so the recheck is overdue as of 2026-09-24 in a 95-year-old on concurrent amiodarone.

71-year-old man (DOB 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation coded 2025-08-22 and listed in the history of all four cardiology clinic notes through 2026-07-28. The only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; no anticoagulant order has ever been placed (a single amiodarone order 2025-08-25 has expired). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3: hypertension (4019), age 65-74, and vascular disease (coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 41401). Oral anticoagulation is recommended. The chart also records 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' (99811, 2025-08-22), which should be weighed when anticoagulation is started but does not remove the indication.

71-year-old woman (DOB 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded 2025-03-14 during the admission for embolic cerebral infarction. Current medications (clinic note 2026-07-10) are carvedilol, metoprolol and famotidine - no anticoagulant, and no anticoagulant order exists in the chart. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: prior stroke (cerebral infarction I639/I6340 with residual hemiplegia I69354, 2 points), hypertension (I10/4019, I129), age 65-74, female sex. Oral anticoagulation is recommended for paroxysmal AF with this score; her ECG of 2025-03-14 being in sinus rhythm does not change the indication. Thrombocytopenia (D696) and history of falling (Z9181) from the same admission should be reviewed when anticoagulation is chosen.

74-year-old man with atrial flutter on apixaban 5 mg twice daily. Outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. At the next clinic visit on 2026-08-20 apixaban was nevertheless re-listed and re-ordered (order dc397aff, valid 2026-08-20 to 2026-12-28) and remains current, together with aspirin and clopidogrel, with no documented review of the bleed or of triple therapy. Anticoagulation should not continue without that review.

Two overlapping oral anticoagulants are current as of 2026-09-24: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (order 7206d5b5, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (order b71a461f, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 clinic note states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was never discontinued and both appear on that visit's medication list. Duplicate anticoagulation markedly increases bleeding risk in a patient with CLL and prior rectal haemorrhage/thrombocytopenia; one agent must be stopped.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 10:55 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded in the chart that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no organised P waves at a ventricular rate of about 139-144/min, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response; unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded that day (Condition 54ec94da) and nursing charting that evening documents AF. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day ECGs and the record needs correction/review.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) is current (order 8de890c6, 2026-04-23 to 2027-01-02; continuously refilled since it was started 2024-05-14). The most recent ECG in the chart, 108018814 of 2023-10-08, shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT about 473 ms and Bazett QTc about 504 ms (>=500 ms), so prescriber review is required per the QT monitoring memo. Note that the 2024-05-14 note starting escitalopram described that same tracing as 'QT acceptable'. Most recent electrolytes are normal: potassium 4.1 mmol/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (both 2025-08-23). No newer ECG is available.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) is current (order 1014aca9, 2026-07-29 to 2027-01-05). The most recent ECG, 106885519 of 2025-11-24, shows sinus rhythm at 62/min with QT about 510 ms and Bazett QTc about 516 ms (>=500 ms), markedly longer than the pre-amiodarone tracing of 2025-06-07 (QTc about 409 ms). Prescriber review is required. Most recent electrolytes (2026-04-20) are normal: potassium 4.4 mmol/L, magnesium 2.2 mg/dL. He also takes warfarin, which amiodarone potentiates.

interpretations.explanation: 2026-03-07. Sinus rhythm at about 81/min with marked phasic (respiratory) RR variation from 658 to 858 ms; an upright uniform P wave (0.15 mV in II, beat-to-beat correlation 0.98) precedes every QRS. PR 178 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT about 325 ms, Bazett QTc about 378 ms. Frontal axis +39 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible; the same-day clinic note 'ECG today: sinus rhythm' agrees with the tracing.

2025-07-15. Sinus tachycardia at about 104/min, regular (RR 570-586 ms), prominent uniform upright P waves with PR 132 ms. QRS 86 ms, QT about 340 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 441 ms. Axis +33 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. The prior tracing of 2025-06-20 was sinus tachycardia at about 147/min with P waves also visible; its QTc measured about 400-430 ms (T-P fusion at that rate makes the estimate imprecise), so no change of 60 ms or more can be established, and there is no new arrhythmia or block.

2024-05-21. Sinus tachycardia at about 110/min with slight rate drift (RR 540-614 ms) and an upright P wave before each QRS (PR about 116 ms); one beat has a deviating P morphology suggesting an atrial premature beat. QRS 84 ms, QT about 320 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 436 ms. Axis +46 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison.

2026-06-10 19:36. Irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia, mean ventricular rate about 140/min (RR 348-648 ms, RMSSD 96 ms) with no organised P waves (P amplitude under 0.06 mV, beat-to-beat P correlation about 0.5) and a fibrillatory baseline - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response; no measurable PR interval. QRS 82 ms, QT about 281 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 436 ms. Axis +10 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. The prior ECG the same day at 17:13 (107914094) was already atrial fibrillation at about 139/min with QTc about 435 ms, so there is no change. Note the 2026-06-10 clinic note describing 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72' conflicts with both tracings.

2025-08-02. Sinus rhythm at about 69/min, regular (RR 864-884 ms), with a consistent P wave before each QRS (PR 136 ms). QRS 76 ms, QT about 396 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 421 ms. Frontal axis about -27 degrees (normal, borderline leftward). No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with 2025-04-27 (sinus about 60/min, PR about 132 ms, QRS 74 ms, QTc about 398 ms) there is no new arrhythmia or block and the QTc change is about 23 ms, less than 60 ms.

2024-05-23. Sinus rhythm at about 97/min, regular (RR 596-628 ms), upright P waves with a short PR of about 110 ms. QRS 70 ms, QT about 297 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 379 ms. Axis about -4 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

2025-12-25. Sinus rhythm at about 72/min, regular (RR 822-840 ms) with a uniform P wave before every QRS, PR about 140 ms. QRS 68 ms, QT about 365 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 394 ms. Axis +20 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart; it predates the escitalopram start of 2026-08-01, so it does not satisfy the post-start monitoring requirement.

2024-11-15. Irregular rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of about 58/min. The RR intervals are bimodal - a dominant regular cycle of about 1130-1165 ms (about 52/min) interrupted by premature beats at 694-906 ms - and averaging only the long-cycle beats shows a completely flat baseline with no P wave in the 300 ms before the QRS (P amplitude under 0.02 mV) and no fibrillatory waves. This is a regular junctional/escape rhythm with frequent premature (atrial and ventricular) beats rather than atrial fibrillation, so the rhythm is classified as OTHER and no PR interval is measurable; concurrent nursing charting that day documented junctional rhythm with PVCs and PACs. QRS 84 ms, QT about 409 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 385 ms, axis +25 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 2024-11-12 (107873952) showed sinus rhythm at 69/min with PR 172 ms and QTc about 389 ms; the loss of sinus P waves is not one of the listed change categories and the QTc is unchanged.

2025-03-09. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus bradycardia at about 58/min (RR 974-1082 ms) with prominent uniform upright P waves and a short PR of about 110 ms. QRS 80 ms, QT about 420-430 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 418 ms. Axis +61 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior day's ECG (106045460: sinus 62/min, PR 110 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc about 443 ms) there is no rhythm or conduction change and the QTc change of about -25 ms is under 60 ms.

2025-08-23. Sinus rhythm at about 83/min, regular (RR 716-728 ms), uniform upright P waves with PR 146 ms. QRS 66 ms, QT about 337 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 397 ms. Axis +55 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

2020-06-19. Sinus rhythm at about 77/min, regular (RR 774-804 ms), with a clear uniform P wave before each QRS (PR 152 ms). QRS 68 ms, QT about 384 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 430 ms, with a well-formed upright T wave. Axis +60 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 2020-02-02 (sinus about 74/min with ventricular ectopy, PR about 140 ms) had a flat, late-terminating T wave with QT about 450 ms and QTc about 500 ms; the QTc has therefore fallen by roughly 65-70 ms, meeting the 60 ms threshold (the prior measurement is less precise because of the low-amplitude T wave).

2021-01-18. Sinus tachycardia at about 121/min, very regular (RR 494-504 ms) with a consistent P wave before each QRS. PR 168 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT about 274 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 388 ms. Axis +53 degrees (normal), no conduction block. Compared with the prior tracing of 2016-09-16 (sinus tachycardia 108/min, PR 174 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc about 394 ms) there is no significant change: no new arrhythmia, no new bundle branch block and QTc differs by only about 6 ms.

2025-06-23. Sinus bradycardia at about 54/min, regular (RR 1074-1118 ms), with a uniform upright P wave before every QRS. The P wave begins about 250 ms and peaks about 205 ms before the QRS onset, giving a PR interval of about 210-214 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS 82 ms (no bundle branch block; tall R in V1-V6 with dominant R in V1), QT about 392 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 373 ms. Axis +11 degrees (normal). Compared with 2024-11-30 (sinus about 51/min, PR about 185 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc about 358 ms) the PR has lengthened slightly but there is no new bundle branch block, no arrhythmia and the QTc change is about 15 ms.

2025-09-13 07:17. Irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia at a mean ventricular rate of about 151/min (RR 288-578 ms, RMSSD 104 ms) with no organised P waves (beat-to-beat P-window correlation about 0.2, P amplitude under 0.02 mV) - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response; no measurable PR interval. QRS 72 ms, QT about 260 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 411 ms. Axis about -9 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 2025-09-12 18:57 (107374881) showed sinus rhythm at about 77/min with P waves and PR about 140 ms (one atrial premature beat), QTc about 409 ms, so this tracing represents NEW atrial fibrillation; AF was coded at this admission and nursing charting that morning recorded AF.

2025-11-23. Sinus rhythm at about 73/min with mild sinus arrhythmia (RR 790-922 ms); prominent uniform upright P waves, PR 168 ms. QRS 80 ms, QT about 350 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 388 ms. Axis +6 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 2025-11-21 (sinus 67/min, PR about 156 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT about 494 ms, QTc about 522 ms) the QTc has fallen by roughly 130 ms, well beyond the 60 ms threshold. The same-day clinic note documenting 'sinus rhythm' is consistent with this tracing.

2025-02-15. Sinus rhythm at about 74/min, regular (RR 800-824 ms), with a uniform P wave before each QRS and a PR interval of about 180 ms (upper normal). QRS 84 ms, QT about 371-382 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 418 ms. Axis +62 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

2023-06-26. Sinus tachycardia at about 112/min, strikingly regular (RR 536-540 ms), with a large uniform P wave before each QRS (PR about 155-160 ms). QRS 86 ms with a very deep S in V1 (about -3 mV), QT about 277-288 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 385 ms. Axis +31 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 2022-07-04 (102955795) is nearly identical (sinus tachycardia 115/min, PR about 165 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc about 380 ms): no new arrhythmia (no AF or flutter on either tracing despite the coded atrial flutter history), no new block and no significant QTc change.

2025-03-14. Underlying sinus rhythm at about 62/min (regular RR about 955-985 ms) with a single early beat and compensatory pause (RR 554 then 1374 ms) - an atrial premature beat; every sinus beat is preceded by a uniform broad P wave with a PR interval of about 195-205 ms (upper limit of normal, not clearly first-degree AV block). QRS 92 ms, QT about 350-375 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 370 ms. Frontal axis about -35 degrees (left axis deviation). No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart. The tracing being in sinus rhythm is compatible with the coded paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (which is not captured on this 10-second recording).

2026-04-29. Sinus rhythm at about 69/min, regular (RR 836-884 ms), with a consistent atrial complex before each QRS and PR about 140 ms. QRS 86 ms, QT about 350 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 376 ms. The QRS is negative in leads I, II and aVL and positive in III with a normal precordial R-wave progression, giving a computed frontal axis of about -170 degrees (extreme/right-superior axis); the negative P and QRS in lead I raise the possibility of left-right arm lead reversal, which should be excluded before accepting this as a true extreme axis. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart; it was obtained 19 days after escitalopram was started (outside the required 14-day window).

2023-11-10. Sinus rhythm at about 70/min with mild rate drift (RR 798-890 ms); a uniform P wave precedes each QRS, PR about 156 ms. QRS 86 ms, QT about 485 ms with a late broad T wave, Bazett QTc about 521 ms - prolonged. Axis +48 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 2020-06-17 (sinus tachycardia about 133/min, PR about 136 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT about 292 ms, QTc about 434 ms) the QTc has increased by roughly 85 ms, more than 60 ms, while taking citalopram 40 mg daily.

2026-03-08. Sinus rhythm at about 68/min, regular (RR 862-902 ms), with a uniform upright P wave before each QRS and PR about 142 ms. QRS 80 ms, QT about 373 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 397 ms - normal, with no evidence of drug-induced QT prolongation on escitalopram. Axis +33 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart; it satisfies the 30-day post-start monitoring requirement for escitalopram begun 2026-02-12.

2019-01-13. Sinus bradycardia at about 53/min with gradual rate slowing (RR 1112-1170 ms); a uniform upright P wave precedes each QRS, PR about 172 ms. QRS 84 ms, QT about 374 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 351 ms. Axis about -16 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with 2018-12-13 (sinus 66/min, PR about 200 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc about 388 ms) there is no new arrhythmia or bundle branch block and the QTc change of about -37 ms is under 60 ms.

2023-10-08. Sinus rhythm at about 68/min (RR 862-902 ms) with a uniform P wave before every QRS. PR 128 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT about 473 ms with a late broad T wave, giving a Bazett QTc of about 504 ms - prolonged. Axis +39 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 2022-11-23 (sinus 75/min, QTc about 356 ms) the QTc has increased by roughly 150 ms, far more than 60 ms, while on escitalopram; this underlies the QT safety review item.

2022-07-13. Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at about 141/min (RR 404-454 ms, RMSSD only 11 ms) with a single uniform atrial wave before each QRS, but that wave is NEGATIVE in leads I, II, aVL and positive in aVR/V1 with a PR of about 130 ms - non-sinus (ectopic low-atrial/junctional) atrial activity at a 1:1 ratio, i.e. ectopic atrial tachycardia rather than sinus tachycardia; there is no sawtooth at 240-340/min to support flutter and no fibrillatory baseline, so the rhythm is classified OTHER. QRS 78 ms, QT about 267 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 409 ms. Axis about -6 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 2022-07-11 (109839112) was atrial fibrillation (RR 380-824 ms, RMSSD 190 ms, no P waves), so the atrial fibrillation present then is no longer present - RESOLVED_AF; QTc is essentially unchanged (about 418 to 409 ms).

2025-05-12. Sinus rhythm at about 82/min, regular (RR 708-748 ms), with a uniform P wave before each QRS and PR about 148 ms. QRS 96 ms - mildly widened but below 120 ms, so no bundle branch block is diagnosed. QT about 367 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 430 ms. Axis +27 degrees (normal). No AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

2022-07-16. Sinus rhythm at about 91/min, very regular (RR 650-666 ms), with a uniform P wave before each QRS (PR about 135-170 ms depending on lead, taken as about 150 ms). QRS 78 ms, QT about 337 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 412 ms. Frontal axis about -46 degrees (left axis deviation). No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with 2021-05-16 (sinus 87/min, PR about 136 ms, QRS 78 ms, QTc about 392 ms, axis +12 degrees) the axis has shifted leftward but there is no new arrhythmia, no new bundle branch block and the QTc change is about 20 ms.

2024-07-17. Sinus rhythm at about 61/min (RR 956-1192 ms, occasional premature beat) with a P wave before each QRS beginning about 275 ms before QRS onset - PR about 210 ms, first-degree AV block. QRS is broad at about 126-130 ms with deep monophasic QS complexes in V1-V2, a broad notched R in I and V6 and absent septal q waves - left bundle branch block. QT about 430 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 433 ms. Frontal axis about -25 degrees (normal, borderline leftward). Compared with the prior ECG of 2024-06-03 (sinus about 68/min, PR about 200 ms, QRS 122 ms with the same LBBB pattern, QTc about 433 ms) the bundle branch block is unchanged (not new), and there is no arrhythmia change or QTc change of 60 ms or more.

2025-03-19. Sinus rhythm at about 101/min, regular (RR 580-596 ms), with prominent uniform upright P waves and PR about 144 ms. QRS 82 ms, QT about 311-328 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 416 ms. Axis +47 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 2025-03-18 (101016166) is essentially the same (sinus 101/min, PR about 132 ms, QRS 78 ms, QTc about 415 ms): no rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

2025-09-22. Sinus rhythm at about 66/min, regular (RR 906-932 ms), with a uniform upright P wave before each QRS and PR about 154 ms. QRS 82 ms, QT about 365 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 382 ms. Frontal axis about -33 degrees (left axis deviation, just beyond the -30 degree limit). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

2022-04-27. Sinus bradycardia at about 58/min (RR 970-1098 ms) with a uniform P wave before each QRS; the P begins about 245 ms and peaks about 205 ms before QRS onset, giving a PR interval of about 200 ms - at the upper limit of normal, not counted as first-degree AV block. QRS 78 ms, QT about 520 ms with a very late T wave, Bazett QTc about 510-525 ms - markedly prolonged (she is on amiodarone). Axis +38 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block. Compared with the prior ECG of 2022-04-06 (100867733: irregularly irregular, mean rate about 130/min, no P waves - atrial fibrillation, QTc about 429 ms), sinus rhythm has been restored (RESOLVED_AF) and the QTc has increased by about 85 ms (>=60 ms).

2022-05-01. Sinus tachycardia at about 107/min, regular (RR 550-564 ms), with prominent uniform upright P waves and PR about 160 ms. QRS 62 ms (narrow), QT about 302-310 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 409 ms. Axis +47 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with 2019-07-27 (sinus 75/min, PR about 158 ms, QRS 64 ms, QTc about 415 ms) there is no new arrhythmia, no new block and essentially no QTc change.

2024-04-19. Sinus tachycardia at about 121/min, regular (RR 490-500 ms), with an upright P wave preceding each narrow QRS. PR 134 ms, QRS 72 ms, QT about 270 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 380 ms. Axis +71 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block, no AV block. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison is possible.

2021-08-23 10:07. Sinus rhythm at about 101/min, regular, uniform upright P waves with PR 144 ms. QRS 82 ms, QT about 312 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 404 ms. Axis +53 degrees (normal), no conduction abnormality. 48-year-old man (DOB 1978-02-27) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation carried in the problem list of every cardiology clinic note from 2025-07-19 to 2026-06-12 (dysrhythmia also coded 2025-06-17). Current medications are famotidine and pantoprazole only; no anticoagulant order is active and none has been ordered since the 2025 admissions. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2: heart failure (congestive heart failure 4280 / acute systolic heart failure 42821 / cardiomyopathy 4254, Feb 2025) and hypertension (4019). A score of 2 in a man is a guideline indication for oral anticoagulation, so the absence of therapy needs review. Note the chart also carries 'long-term current use of anticoagulants' (V5861, Jun 2025), which is not supported by any active order.

The anticoagulation clinic note of 2026-09-10 by L. Nguyen, PharmD documents a dose change made under the clinic protocol: home INR 3.4, warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily. A clinic pharmacist dose change after 2026-03-01 requires an INR within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-17. No INR has been resulted since 2026-08-22 (2.6), so the recheck is overdue as of 2026-09-24 in a 95-year-old on concurrent amiodarone.

71-year-old man (DOB 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation coded 2025-08-22 and listed in the history of all four cardiology clinic notes through 2026-07-28. The only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; no anticoagulant order has ever been placed (a single amiodarone order 2025-08-25 has expired). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3: hypertension (4019), age 65-74, and vascular disease (coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 41401). Oral anticoagulation is recommended. The chart also records 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' (99811, 2025-08-22), which should be weighed when anticoagulation is started but does not remove the indication.

71-year-old woman (DOB 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded 2025-03-14 during the admission for embolic cerebral infarction. Current medications (clinic note 2026-07-10) are carvedilol, metoprolol and famotidine - no anticoagulant, and no anticoagulant order exists in the chart. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: prior stroke (cerebral infarction I639/I6340 with residual hemiplegia I69354, 2 points), hypertension (I10/4019, I129), age 65-74, female sex. Oral anticoagulation is recommended for paroxysmal AF with this score; her ECG of 2025-03-14 being in sinus rhythm does not change the indication. Thrombocytopenia (D696) and history of falling (Z9181) from the same admission should be reviewed when anticoagulation is chosen.

74-year-old man with atrial flutter on apixaban 5 mg twice daily. Outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. At the next clinic visit on 2026-08-20 apixaban was nevertheless re-listed and re-ordered (order dc397aff, valid 2026-08-20 to 2026-12-28) and remains current, together with aspirin and clopidogrel, with no documented review of the bleed or of triple therapy. Anticoagulation should not continue without that review.

Two overlapping oral anticoagulants are current as of 2026-09-24: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (order 7206d5b5, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (order b71a461f, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 clinic note states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was never discontinued and both appear on that visit's medication list. Duplicate anticoagulation markedly increases bleeding risk in a patient with CLL and prior rectal haemorrhage/thrombocytopenia; one agent must be stopped.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 10:55 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded in the chart that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no organised P waves at a ventricular rate of about 139-144/min, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response; unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded that day (Condition 54ec94da) and nursing charting that evening documents AF. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day ECGs and the record needs correction/review.

interpretations.explanation: 2026-03-07. Sinus rhythm at about 81/min with marked phasic (respiratory) RR variation from 658 to 858 ms; an upright uniform P wave (0.15 mV in II, beat-to-beat correlation 0.98) precedes every QRS. PR 178 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT about 325 ms, Bazett QTc about 378 ms. Frontal axis +39 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible; the same-day clinic note 'ECG today: sinus rhythm' agrees with the tracing.

arguments.explanation: 2021-01-18. Sinus tachycardia at about 121/min, very regular (RR 494-504 ms) with a consistent P wave before each QRS. PR 168 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT about 274 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 388 ms. Axis +53 degrees (normal), no conduction block. Compared with the prior tracing of 2016-09-16 (sinus tachycardia 108/min, PR 174 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc about 394 ms) there is no significant change: no new arrhythmia, no new bundle branch block and QTc differs by only about 6 ms.

CHA2DS2-VASc = 2: heart failure (congestive heart failure 4280 / acute systolic heart failure 42821 / cardiomyopathy 4254, Feb 2025) and hypertension (4019). A score of 2 in a man is a guideline indication for oral anticoagulation, so the absence of therapy needs review. Note the chart also carries 'long-term current use of anticoagulants' (V5861, Jun 2025), which is not supported by any active order.

The anticoagulation clinic note of 2026-09-10 by L. Nguyen, PharmD documents a dose change made under the clinic protocol: home INR 3.4, warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily. A clinic pharmacist dose change after 2026-03-01 requires an INR within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-17. No INR has been resulted since 2026-08-22 (2.6), so the recheck is overdue as of 2026-09-24 in a 95-year-old on concurrent amiodarone.

71-year-old man (DOB 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation coded 2025-08-22 and listed in the history of all four cardiology clinic notes through 2026-07-28. The only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; no anticoagulant order has ever been placed (a single amiodarone order 2025-08-25 has expired). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3: hypertension (4019), age 65-74, and vascular disease (coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 41401). Oral anticoagulation is recommended. 71-year-old woman (DOB 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded 2025-03-14 during the admission for embolic cerebral infarction. Current medications (clinic note 2026-07-10) are carvedilol, metoprolol and famotidine - no anticoagulant, and no anticoagulant order exists in the chart. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: prior stroke (cerebral infarction I639/I6340 with residual hemiplegia I69354, 2 points), hypertension (I10/4019, I129), age 65-74, female sex. Oral anticoagulation is recommended for paroxysmal AF with this score; her ECG of 2025-03-14 being in sinus rhythm does not change the indication. Thrombocytopenia (D696) and history of falling (Z9181) from the same admission should be reviewed when anticoagulation is chosen.

74-year-old man with atrial flutter on apixaban 5 mg twice daily. Outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. At the next clinic visit on 2026-08-20 apixaban was nevertheless re-listed and re-ordered (order dc397aff, valid 2026-08-20 to 2026-12-28) and remains current, together with aspirin and clopidogrel, with no documented review of the bleed or of triple therapy. Anticoagulation should not continue without that review.

Two overlapping oral anticoagulants are current as of 2026-09-24: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (order 7206d5b5, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (order b71a461f, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 clinic note states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was never discontinued and both appear on that visit's medication list. Duplicate anticoagulation markedly increases bleeding risk in a patient with CLL and prior rectal haemorrhage/thrombocytopenia; one agent must be stopped.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 10:55 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded in the chart that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no organised P waves at a ventricular rate of about 139-144/min, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response; unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded that day (Condition 54ec94da) and nursing charting that evening documents AF. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day ECGs and the record needs correction/review.

Most recent electrolytes are normal: potassium 4.1 mmol/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (both 2025-08-23). No newer ECG is available.

2025-07-15. Sinus tachycardia at about 104/min, regular (RR 570-586 ms), prominent uniform upright P waves with PR 132 ms. QRS 86 ms, QT about 340 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 441 ms. The prior tracing of 2025-06-20 was sinus tachycardia at about 147/min with P waves also visible; its QTc measured about 400-430 ms (T-P fusion at that rate makes the estimate imprecise), so no change of 60 ms or more can be established, and there is no new arrhythmia or block.

2026-06-10 19:36. Compared with 2025-04-27 (sinus about 60/min, PR about 132 ms, QRS 74 ms, QTc about 398 ms) there is no new arrhythmia or block and the QTc change is about 23 ms, less than 60 ms.

2024-05-23. Sinus rhythm at about 97/min, regular (RR 596-628 ms), upright P waves with a short PR of about 110 ms. QRS 70 ms, QT about 297 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 379 ms. Axis about -4 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

2025-12-25. Sinus rhythm at about 72/min, regular (RR 822-840 ms) with a uniform P wave before every QRS, PR about 140 ms. QRS 68 ms, QT about 365 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 394 ms. 2024-11-15. Irregular rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of about 58/min. This is a regular junctional/escape rhythm with frequent premature (atrial and ventricular) beats rather than atrial fibrillation, so the rhythm is classified as OTHER and no PR interval is measurable; concurrent nursing charting that day documented junctional rhythm with PVCs and PACs. QRS 84 ms, QT about 409 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 385 ms, axis +25 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 2024-11-12 (107873952) showed sinus rhythm at 69/min with PR 172 ms and QTc about 389 ms; the loss of sinus P waves is not one of the listed change categories and the QTc is unchanged.

Compared with the prior day's ECG (106045460: sinus 62/min, PR 110 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc about 443 ms) there is no rhythm or conduction change and the QTc change of about -25 ms is under 60 ms.

Compared with the earlier ECG the same day (106516875: sinus tachycardia 100/min, PR 136 ms, QTc about 447 ms) there is no new arrhythmia or block and the QTc change (about -41 ms) is less than 60 ms.

Compared with the prior ECG of 2025-06-07 (sinus bradyarrhythmia about 47-50/min, PR about 180 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc about 409 ms) the QTc has risen by roughly 105 ms after amiodarone was started - a change of 60 ms or more.

2024-09-17. Only ECG in the chart; atrial fibrillation was coded at the same admission (2024-09-16) and he is anticoagulated with warfarin.

2025-08-02. Sinus rhythm at about 69/min, regular (RR 864-884 ms), with a consistent P wave before each QRS (PR 136 ms). QRS 76 ms, QT about 396 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 421 ms. Compared with 2025-04-27 (sinus about 60/min, PR about 132 ms, QRS 74 ms, QTc about 398 ms) there is no new arrhythmia or block and the QTc change is about 23 ms, less than 60 ms.

2024-05-23. Sinus rhythm at about 97/min, regular (RR 596-628 ms), upright P waves with a short PR of about 110 ms. QRS 70 ms, QT about 297 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 379 ms. Axis about -4 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

2025-12-25. Sinus rhythm at about 72/min, regular (RR 822-840 ms) with a uniform P wave before every QRS, PR about 140 ms. QRS 68 ms, QT about 365 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 394 ms. Axis +20 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart; it predates the escitalopram start of 2026-08-01, so it does not satisfy the post-start monitoring requirement.

2024-11-15. Irregular rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of about 58/min. QRS 84 ms, QT about 409 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 385 ms, axis +25 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 2024-11-12 (107873952) showed sinus rhythm at 69/min with PR 172 ms and QTc about 389 ms; the loss of sinus P waves is not one of the listed change categories and the QTc is unchanged.

2025-03-09. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus bradycardia at about 58/min (RR 974-1082 ms) with prominent uniform upright P waves and a short PR of about 110 ms. QRS 80 ms, QT about 420-430 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 418 ms. Axis +61 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior day's ECG (106045460: sinus 62/min, PR 110 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc about 443 ms) there is no rhythm or conduction change and the QTc change of about -25 ms is under 60 ms.

2025-08-23. Sinus rhythm at about 83/min, regular (RR 716-728 ms), uniform upright P waves with PR 146 ms. QRS 66 ms, QT about 337 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 397 ms. Axis +55 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

QRS 68 ms, QT about 384 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 430 ms, with a well-formed upright T wave. Axis +60 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Axis +53 degrees (normal), no conduction block. Compared with the prior tracing of 2016-09-16 (sinus tachycardia 108/min, PR 174 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc about 394 ms) there is no significant change: no new arrhythmia, no new bundle branch block and QTc differs by only about 6 ms.

PR 128 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT about 473 ms with a late broad T wave, giving a Bazett QTc of about 504 ms - prolonged. Axis +39 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 2022-11-23 (sinus 75/min, QTc about 356 ms) the QTc has increased by roughly 150 ms, far more than 60 ms, while on escitalopram; this underlies the QT safety review item.

2024-04-19. Sinus tachycardia at about 121/min, regular (RR 490-500 ms), with an upright P wave preceding each narrow QRS. PR 134 ms, QRS 72 ms, QT about 270 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 380 ms. Axis +71 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block, no AV block. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison is possible.

2021-08-23 10:07. Sinus rhythm at about 101/min, regular, uniform upright P waves with PR 144 ms. QRS 82 ms, QT about 312 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 404 ms. Axis +53 degrees (normal), no conduction abnormality. The prior tracing 34 seconds earlier (102910502) is essentially identical (sinus 100/min, PR 142 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc about 401 ms): no rhythm change, no new block, QTc change about 3 ms.

2024-10-24. Sinus bradycardia at about 52/min, regular (RR 1144-1178 ms), with a low-amplitude but consistent P wave before each QRS (PR 172 ms). QRS 84 ms, tall precordial voltages, QT about 410-425 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 385 ms. Axis +34 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with 2023-05-22 (sinus about 57/min with one premature beat, PR about 155 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc about 375 ms) there is no significant change - QTc within 15 ms, no new AF and no new block.

2024-12-05 14:38. Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at about 122/min (RR 492-496 ms) with a constant P wave before every QRS (PR 126 ms) - sinus tachycardia. QRS 80 ms, QT about 289 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 406 ms. The frontal QRS axis computes to about -178 degrees (net QRS negative in lead I, isoelectric in aVF), i.e. a right-superior/extreme axis sitting on the right-versus-extreme border; with negative P and QRS in lead I and normal precordial progression, limb-lead reversal should be excluded. No bundle branch block. Compared with the earlier ECG the same day (106516875: sinus tachycardia 100/min, PR 136 ms, QTc about 447 ms) there is no new arrhythmia or block and the QTc change (about -41 ms) is less than 60 ms.

2025-11-24. Sinus rhythm at about 62/min (RR 944-982 ms) with a low-amplitude P wave before each QRS, PR about 168 ms. QRS 90 ms. The T wave is very late (peak about 390 ms after the R wave) with QT about 510 ms and Bazett QTc about 516 ms - markedly prolonged. Axis +65 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block, no AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 2025-06-07 (sinus bradyarrhythmia about 47-50/min, PR about 180 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc about 409 ms) the QTc has risen by roughly 105 ms after amiodarone was started - a change of 60 ms or more.

2024-09-17. Irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of about 100/min (RR 408-1070 ms, RMSSD 250 ms, no repeating pattern) with no organised P waves (median P amplitude under 0.02 mV, beat-to-beat P correlation about 0.5) - atrial fibrillation, so there is no measurable PR interval. QRS 76 ms, QT about 317 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 405 ms. Frontal axis about -60 degrees (left axis deviation). No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart; atrial fibrillation was coded at the same admission (2024-09-16) and he is anticoagulated with warfarin.

Anticoagulation should not continue without that review.

Two overlapping oral anticoagulants are current as of 2026-09-24: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (order 7206d5b5, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (order b71a461f, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 clinic note states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was never discontinued and both appear on that visit's medication list. Duplicate anticoagulation markedly increases bleeding risk in a patient with CLL and prior rectal haemorrhage/thrombocytopenia; one agent must be stopped.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 10:55 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded in the chart that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no organised P waves at a ventricular rate of about 139-144/min, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response; unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded that day (Condition 54ec94da) and nursing charting that evening documents AF. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day ECGs and the record needs correction/review.

Most recent electrolytes are normal: potassium 4.1 mmol/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (both 2025-08-23). No newer ECG is available.

The 2026-07-15 clinic note states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was never discontinued and both appear on that visit's medication list. Duplicate anticoagulation markedly increases bleeding risk in a patient with CLL and prior rectal haemorrhage/thrombocytopenia; one agent must be stopped.
